tooltip.relicera.astral_storybook.empty: §9A magical book that can meddle with dreams. When combined with certain items, related stories will emerge.
toast.relicera.astral_storybook_read.des: A particular dream will come tonight.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.0: Once upon a time, a little tailor lived in a tiny attic.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.1: One day, while eating jam, several flies buzzed over. He swung a cloth and killed seven in one blow.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.2: Proud of himself, the tailor embroidered "Seven at One Blow!!" on his belt.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.3: Wearing the belt, he left his little town.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.4: Everyone he met thought he had slain seven men in one blow.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.5: On the road, a giant blocked his way and challenged him to a test of strength.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.6: The tailor passed off cheese as a stone and squeezed water from it. Then he released a bird from his pocket, making the giant think he had thrown a stone so high it never came back.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.8: Later, the tailor reached the royal palace. The king asked him to deal with giants, a unicorn, and a wild boar.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.9: Using his wits, the tailor tricked the giants into fighting each other, made the unicorn charge into a tree, and trapped the boar.
storybook.relicera.1.paragraph.10: At last, everyone believed the little tailor truly possessed extraordinary courage.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.0: A young soldier had nowhere to go when the Devil appeared before him.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.1: "I can give you endless riches, but on one condition."
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.2: For seven years, the soldier could not wash, pray, or remove the bearskin he wore.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.3: "If you die within those seven years, your soul is mine."
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.4: The soldier agreed. Wrapped in the bearskin, he began his long seven years.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.5: Year after year, people fled at the sight of him, and children cried in fear.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.6: Yet his pockets never ran out of gold.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.7: The soldier always helped the poor. He asked only one thing: "Please pray for me."
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.8: In gratitude, a merchant offered him one of his daughters in marriage.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.9: The two older daughters feared him, but the youngest agreed.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.10: The soldier broke a ring in half, giving one piece to the girl and keeping the other.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.11: When the seventh year ended, the Devil kept his word.
storybook.relicera.2.paragraph.12: The soldier married the youngest daughter, and their wedding bells rang far and wide.
